verses.sanskrit:
शौनक उवाच।
              आख्याता भुजगास्तात वीर्यवन्तो दुरासदाः। शापं तं तेऽभिविज्ञाय कृतवन्तः किमुत्तरम्॥१॥
verses.english: Shaunaka said: O child, you have told us of many greatly powerful and unconquerable serpents. What did they do after hearing of the curse?

verses.sanskrit:
सौतिरुवाच।
              तेषां तु भगवाञ्च्छेषः कद्रूं त्यक्त्वा महायशाः। उग्रं तपः समातस्थे वायुभक्षो यतव्रतः॥२॥
verses.english: Sauti said: Illustrious and famous Shesha, having left (his mother) Kadru, practised austere penances, living on air and rigidly observing vows.
verses.bhavadeepa: षट्त्रिंशः अध्यायः पित्र्याचार्यादिभ्यः पूज्यतमापि माताऽनृताभिसम्बन्धिनी चेत्याज्यैवेति दर्शयितुं शेषाध्यायमारभते। आख्याता इत्यादिना उत्तरमनन्तरम्॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: गन्धमादनमासाद्य बदर्यां च तपोरतः। गोकर्णे पुष्करारण्ये तथा हिमवतस्तटे॥३॥
verses.english: He practised his penances, going to Gandhamadana, Badari, Gokarna, the forest of Pushkara and the foot of the Himalayas.

verses.sanskrit: तेषु तेषु च पुण्येषु तीर्थेष्वायतनेषु च। एकान्तशीलो नियतः सततं विजितेन्द्रियः॥४॥
verses.english: He passed his days in these sacred places, rigidly observing his vows, completely controlling his passions and concentrating his mind.

verses.sanskrit: तप्यमानं तपो घोरं तं ददर्श पितामहः। संशुष्कमांसत्वक्स्नायुं जटाचीरधरं मुनिम्॥५॥
verses.english: The Grandsire saw him with knotted hair, clad in rags, his flesh, skin and sinews dried up owing to the austere penances he was practising.

verses.sanskrit: तमब्रवीत्सत्यधृतिं तप्यमानं पितामहः। किमिदं कुरुषे शेष प्रजानां स्वस्ति वै कुरु॥६॥
verses.english: The Grandsire, addressing that penancepractising ascetic, said, “O Shesha, what are you doing? let the welfare of the worlds also engage your thoughts.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं हि तीव्रेण तपसा प्रजास्तापयसेऽनघ। ब्रूहि कामं च मे शेष यस्ते हृदि व्यवस्थितः॥७॥
verses.english: O sinless one, you are giving pain to all creatures by your austere penances. O Shesha, tell me the desire of your mind."

verses.sanskrit:
शेष उवाच।
              सोदर्या मम सर्वे हि भ्रातरो मन्दचेतसः। सह तैर्नोत्सहे वस्तुं तद्भवाननुमन्यताम्॥८॥
verses.english: Shesha said: My brothers are all of wicked hearts. I do not wish to live with them. Kindly sanction this.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्यसूयन्ति सततं परस्परममित्रवत्। ततोऽहं तप आतिष्ठं नैतन्पश्येयमित्युत॥९॥
verses.english: They are jealous of one another like great enemies. I am, therefore, engaged in penances. I shall not even see them.

verses.sanskrit: न मर्षयन्ति ससुतां सततं विनतां च ते। अस्माकं चापरो भ्राता वैनतेयोऽन्तरिक्षगः॥१०॥
verses.english: They never show any kindness for Vinata and her son, who is our other brother, the bird of the air.

verses.sanskrit: तं च द्विषन्ति सततं स चापि बलवत्तरः। वरप्रदानात्स पितुः कश्यपस्य महात्मनः॥११॥
verses.english: They always envy him. He too is much stronger than (all of us), owing to the boon granted by our father, the illustrious and noble Kashyapa.

verses.sanskrit: सोऽहं तपः समास्थाय मोक्ष्यामीदं कलेवरम्। कथं मे प्रेत्यभावेऽपि न तैः स्यात्सह सङ्गमः॥१२॥
verses.english: Therefore, I am practising penances and I shall cast off this body of mine, so that I may not any association with them even after death.

verses.sanskrit: तमेवं वादिनं शेषं पितामह उवाच ह। जानामि शेष सर्वेषां भ्रातॄणां ते विचेष्टितम्॥१३॥
verses.english: Sauti said : When Shesha thus spoke, the Grandsire told him, "O Shesha, I know the character of your brothers.

verses.sanskrit: मातुश्चाप्यपराधाद्वै भ्रातॄणां ते महद्भयम्। कृतोऽत्र परिहारश्च पूर्वमेव भुजङ्गम॥१४॥
verses.english: (And I know also) their great danger owing to their offence against their mother. O snake, a remedy has been already provided by me.

verses.sanskrit: भ्रातॄणां तव सर्वेषां न शोकं कर्तुमर्हसि। वृणीष्व च वरं मत्तः शेष यत्तेऽभिकाङ्क्षितम्॥१५॥
verses.english: You should not grieve for your brothers. O Shesha, whatever you desire to possess, ask it from me.

verses.sanskrit: दास्यामि हि वरं तेऽद्य प्रीतिर्मे परमा त्वयि। दिष्ट्या बुद्धिश्च ते धर्मे निविष्टा पन्नगोत्तम। भूयो भूयश्च ते बुद्धिर्धर्मे भवतु सुस्थिरा॥१६॥
verses.english: I am highly pleased with you and I shall grant you a boon today. O best of snakes, it is very good that your heart has been set on virtue. Let your heart be more and more firmly set on virtue."

verses.sanskrit:
शेष उवाच।
              एष एव वरो देव काङ्क्षितो मे पितामह। धर्मे मे रमतां बुद्धिः शमे तपसि चेश्वर॥१७॥
verses.english: Shesha said: Odivine Grandsire, O lord of all, I ask this boon. Let my heart always delight in virtue and in blessed penances.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मोवाच।
              प्रीतोऽस्म्यनेन ते शेष दमेन च शमेन च। त्वया त्विदं वचः कार्यं मन्नियोगात्प्रजाहितम्॥१८॥
verses.english: Brahma said :: O Shesha, I am highly pleased with your self-denial and love of peace. By my command let the following act be done by you for the good of all creatures.
verses.bhavadeepa: धर्मे वेदबोधितेऽर्थे शमे मनोजये तपसि तत्त्वालोचने॥१७॥

verses.sanskrit: इमां महीं शैलवनोपपन्नां ससागरग्रामविहारपत्तनाम्। त्वं शेष सम्यक् चलितां यथावत्संगृह्य तिष्ठस्व यथाऽचला स्यात्॥१९॥
verses.english: Bearing properly and well, this earth which is so very unsteady, towns retreats and seas, with all her mountains and forests with her O Shesha, remain in the way as she may be steady.
verses.bhavadeepa: दमेन बाह्येन्द्रियजयेन प्रश्रयेण चेति पाठे प्रश्रयो विनयः॥१८॥

verses.sanskrit:
शेष उवाच।
              यथाऽऽह देवो वरदः प्रजापतिर्महीपतिर्भूतपतिर्जगत्पतिः। तथा महीं धारयिताऽस्मि निश्चलां प्रयच्छतां मे विवरं प्रजापते॥२०॥
verses.english: Shesha said: O divine lord of all creatures, O granter of boons, O lord of the earth,O the lord of every created thing, O the lord of the universe, I shall hold the earth steady, as you command. O Prajapati, place it upon my head.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मोवाच।
              अधो महीं गच्छ भुजङ्गमोत्तम स्वयं तवैषा विवरं प्रदास्यति। इमां धरां धारयता त्वया हि मे महत्प्रियं शेष कृतं भविष्यति॥२१॥
verses.english: Brahma said: O best of snakes, go underneath the earth. She herself will make a passage for you. O Shesha, you will certainly do what is highly valued by me by holding the earth (on your head.)

verses.sanskrit:
सौतिरुवाच।
              तथैव कृत्वा विवरं प्रविश्य स प्रभुर्भुवो भुजगवराग्रजः स्थितः। बिभर्ति देवीं शिरसा महीमिमां समुद्रनेमिं परिगृह्य सर्वतः॥२२॥
verses.english: Sauti said: The elder brother of the king of the snakes, entering into a hole, went to the other side of the earth. He held that goddess (earth) with her belt of seas all around her.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मोवाच।
              शेषोऽसि नागोत्तम धर्मदेवो महीमिमां धारयसे यदेकः। अनन्तभोगैः परिगृह्य सर्वां यथाहमेवं बलभिद्यथा वा॥२३॥
verses.english: Brahma said: O Shesha, O best of snakes, you are the Dharma, because you hold the earth alone with your infinite hoods, with every thing on her, what I myself and Indra can do.

verses.sanskrit:
सौतिरुवाच।
              अधो भूमौ वसत्येवं नागोऽनन्तः प्रतापवान्। धास्यन्वसुधामेकः शासनाद्ब्रह्मणो विभोः॥२४॥
verses.english: Sauti said: Thus does the snake, Shesha, the greatly powerful lord Ananta, lives underneath the earth, alone supporting the world at the command of Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: सुपर्णं च सहायं वै भगवानमरोत्तमः। प्रादादनन्ताय तदा वैनतेयं पितामहः॥२५॥
verses.english: Then the Grandsire, the illustrious lord of the immortals, gave Suparna (Garuda), the son of Vinata as Ananta's help.
